records.subject: mathematics
records.title: 0580 Paper 1 variant response roles

dimensions.observation: The Venn tasks use both element-level and count-level representations. Variant12 asks ten elements to be placed, then intersection elements and complement cardinality; variants11 and13 ask missing region counts. In11 Q24(c) and13 Q23(b)(ii), the requested outside-event response can be obtained from already supplied regions without relying on the missing-region computation. Source locators: QP11 p14 / MS11 p9; QP12 p12 / MS12 p9; QP13 p13 / MS13 p9.

Stem-and-leaf work varies between constructing ordered data and interpreting an already complete display. Variant11 supplies a median target to justify, variant12 asks how adding one datum changes the median, and variant13 asks a median mass. A numeric answer alone does not satisfy the proof/explanation variants. Source locators: QP11 p9 / MS11 pp7–8; QP12 p6 / MS12 p7; QP13 p6 / MS13 p7.

Transformation prompts consistently require one mapping or one drawn image, but their completeness criteria differ: a rotation needs angle/direction and centre, a translation its vector, and an enlargement centre and factor. Separate parts in11 and12 start again from the original shape rather than compose transformations. Source locators: QP11 p12 / MS11 p8; QP12 p11 / MS12 pp8–9; QP13 p12 / MS13 p8.

uncertainties: Provisional synthesis of three October/November2025 variants only; no cross-session frequency, importance ranking, difficulty claim or lab idea approval inferred.
Marks and follow-through conventions remain question-specific, including11 Q21(a) alternative rotation and13 Q26(b) MS interpretation of neither stopping.

records.subject: mathematics
records.title: Supplied information and response roles in stationary-point tasks

dimensions.observation: 0580/21 Q23 supplies a complete quadratic. 9709/12 Q5 supplies a second derivative and both coordinates of two minima, which constrain an unknown curve. 9709/21 Q7 supplies the full double-angle trigonometric curve plus a shaded-region sketch and names the two maximum x-values α and β. 9709/31 Q6(a) supplies an exponential/trigonometric curve, cos x ≠ 0 and the target stationary-point equation tan x = x + 2. The P3 target is given, so this evidence does not support a rule that later components always supply less.

0580/21 Q23 requests one coordinate pair in a printed two-coordinate template. 9709/12 Q5 also asks for one coordinate pair, but p and integration constants are intermediate unknowns. P2 Q7 asks for one exact area: maximum x-values are intermediate bounds, not separately requested final coordinates. P3 Q6(a) requests a derivation of the supplied equation, not stationary coordinates or a numerical root; later compulsory parts pursue the root.

0580/21 Q23 prints a quadratic and unruled working space with one coordinate-pair template. P1/12 Q5 prints a second derivative and minima without a graph, with responses in a separate answer booklet. P2/21 Q7 supplies a shaded curve and dashed vertical boundaries at α and β. P3/31 Q6(a) supplies symbolic data and ruled working lines without a curve plot. These are observations of these variants, not component-wide layout rules.

0580 syllabus p41 supports quadratic turning points by completing the square (E2.11) and elementary polynomial differentiation/stationary points (E2.12); the Q23 MS accepts multiple methods. P1 syllabus p22 supports integration constants and stationary points: Q5 integrates twice and uses supplied point conditions. P2 Q7 uses differentiation to derive integration bounds before finding an exact trigonometric area. P3 Q6(a) differentiates a composite exponential/trigonometric product, or uses the MS logarithmic route, and rearranges to the supplied equation. Shared stationarity does not make the surrounding operations equivalent.

0580 Q23 awards full marks for the coordinate pair with alternative partial routes. P1/12 Q5 makes all marks after the first stationarity-method mark dependent on using both given x-values in the integrated derivative with its constant; later marks credit second integration and point substitution. P2 Q7 credits derivative, maximum locations, integrand rewriting and exact definite integration. P3 Q6(a) credits derivative and valid derivation of the supplied equation, accepting product-rule or logarithmic differentiation routes. These are scheme-specific requirements, not a universal working ladder.

The sampled 0580 item is Extended non-calculator. The P1, P2 and P3 samples permit calculators, yet ask respectively for curve reconstruction, exact area and symbolic proof. Calculator permission alone does not describe the demanded response.

Within P1, /11 Q10(a) explicitly prescribes second-derivative classification of a supplied point; (b) asks for curve reconstruction; (c)(i) provides an optional factorisation identity for other stationary x-values; (c)(ii) asks their nature and the MS requires evaluated second derivatives. /12 Q5 instead combines second-derivative reconstruction and supplied minima into a single request for the other coordinate pair. The /11 scaffold supplies more named subtasks and an optional identity, but its other-point output asks only x-values, unlike /12’s coordinate pair.

uncertainties: One task per cited component; no frequency, difficulty or Core comparison is inferred.
9709 P1 contributes to AS/A Pure, P2 is AS-only and P3 contributes to A Level Pure; this is not the full A Level qualification.
Concept classification and any interactive-lab design remain provisional.

records.subject: mathematics
records.title: 0580 and 9709 Pure trigonometric equation demand

dimensions.observation: The sampled 0580 Extended non-calculator item states a degree interval. Within 9709 Pure, the P1 equation and P3 root sequence use radians, whereas the P2 phase-form item uses degrees. This sample therefore supports variation within 9709, not a blanket rule that 9709 questions use radians.
uncertainties: This is a bounded paper sample, not an exam-wide frequency claim.

dimensions.observation: The 0580 item begins directly with tan x = -1/sqrt(3); reference-angle/sign reasoning is a plausible route to its two interval answers. The sampled 9709 tasks vary: P1 converts a mixed-power equation into a quadratic in sin^2 theta or cos^2 theta; P2 creates R cos(theta-alpha), then explicitly reuses it in a Hence solution part; P3 supplies tan x = x + 2 as the target to prove from differentiation, then prompts graphical justification of given uniqueness, bracketing and iteration. The target equation is disclosed; its derivation is required. These are observed structures, not a universal difficulty ladder. Within P1, 9709/12 Q6 instead supplies an inverse-cosine equation already containing a quadratic in sin x: inverse-relation conversion replaces P1/11 Q4’s Pythagorean identity substitution. Both routes still require complete interval enumeration.

Neither the 0580 equation nor the 9709 P1/P2 phase-form item supplies a graph. P2 Q7 supplies y = 3 + sin^2(2x) - cos(2x), a labelled curve, dashed vertical boundaries at α and β and a shaded region; the limit values must be recovered. P3 Q6(b) instead prompts a suitable pair of sketches to justify the given only-one-root conclusion; y = tan x and y = x + 2 is the MS-supported choice, not a pair named in the QP. Diagram use varies with the sampled task.
uncertainties: No claim is made that diagrams occur in every P2 or P3 trigonometry question.

dimensions.observation: 0580/21 Q26 has substantial unruled working space followed by two answer blanks; its MS awards full credit for both correct answers, with alternative partial credits for one solution or a reference-angle observation. The sampled 9709/11 P1 item provides a full ruled page and awards identity substitution, quadratic solution and interval enumeration. P3 distributes work over four dependent parts: prove a supplied target equation, justify a supplied uniqueness conclusion using learner-selected sketches, bracket the root and record iterates. These are layouts and demands of the cited variants, not component-wide working-space rules. Within the same P1 component, variant 12 uses a separate answer booklet rather than variant 11’s ruled response page; Q6’s MS explicitly warns that final answers alone do not imply full marks.
uncertainties: 9709 P1/P2/P3 papers all allow calculators, while this particular 0580 item is Extended Paper 2 non-calculator; no causal claim about working space and calculator status is made.

dimensions.observation: The reviewed 0580 MS awards full three marks for both correct solutions; B2 for one correct answer OR B1 for a reference-angle observation are alternative partial credits, not a required/additive chain. The reviewed 9709 P1 MS credits identity conversion, a valid quadratic route and complete radian enumeration. The reviewed P3 MS credits a derivative, the pair y = tan x and y = x + 2 with justification, endpoint calculations and accuracy-justified iteration; degree-mode work earns no marks in parts (c)-(d). P1/12 Q6 credits inverse conversion, both sine values and three radian solutions; unlike the cited 0580 direct equation, its MS explicitly requires more than correct final answers alone. P2 Q4(b) credits use of their part (a) phase form and methods for both interval angles.
uncertainties: Method patterns are restricted to the listed reviewed schemes.

dimensions.observation: 0580/21 Q26 prints two x = slots requiring both solutions of one degree-valued unknown. 9709/11 Q4 asks to solve for one radian-valued theta without specifying a solution count; four solutions are derived, not four printed blanks. 9709/21 Q4(a) requests two distinct parameters (dimensionless R and degree-valued alpha), both required; (b) reuses them to solve for all interval values of theta on ruled lines without fixed answer slots. 9709/31 Q6(a-d) comprises four compulsory tasks about one root: supplied targets require proof/sketch justification, then a supplied bracket requires calculations and the final root requires recorded iterates. Printed subpart labels do not name extra unknowns or imply choice. P1/12 Q6 also leaves the solution count unstated: two intermediate sine values yield three radian x values, with no printed response slots.

Additional Pure items show varied transformations even within component: P2/21 Q2(a) solves a modulus equation and (b) reuses its roots as cotangent values, although the MS permits restarting. P3/31 Q5(a) proves a supplied reciprocal/double-angle identity and (b) explicitly reuses it to enumerate two radian solutions; degree answers receive a specific misread concession here, unlike the zero-credit degree-mode rule for Q6(c-d). These local marking differences must not become a universal radian-method rule.

uncertainties: The comparison covers selected 0580 Extended and 9709 Pure items only; it is not a Core-versus-AS/A or full-qualification comparison.
9709 A Level Pure scope includes P1 and P3, but full A Level qualification also has applied components outside this evidence project.

records.subject: mathematics
records.title: 0580 Core and Extended calculator rounding-bound responses

dimensions.observation: Both cited covers permit a scientific calculator where appropriate; this common condition does not imply identical task operations.

P3/31 Q22(b), QP15, supplies the inequality symbols and asks two endpoints for a distance rounded to 97 km. P4/42 Q20, QP15, asks one lower volume bound from rounded mass 4810 g and density 7.7 g/cm³; the mass/density endpoints are unprompted intermediates. Two answer slots are therefore not evidence of greater demand than one.

P3 recovers a half-unit rounding interval, 96.5≤d<97.5. P4 rearranges the supplied density relation, selects the lower mass and upper density, and computes 4805/7.75=620 cm³. These are two reviewed source tasks, not a route-wide hierarchy.

MS31 p9 awards one mark for each endpoint in its correct position, with one special-case mark if both are reversed after zero. MS42 p10 awards three for 620 not from wrong working; its M2 and M1 alternatives recognise partial control of the quotient bounds. Neither scheme requires an invented universal chain.

uncertainties: Parent checked both rendered QPs and MS rows. This bounded comparison does not establish route-wide difficulty, calculator causality or syllabus exclusion.

dimensions.observation: All three source covers require non-calculator work, necessary working, geometrical instruments and supplied formulas. This is a component condition, not evidence that every task needs the same method.

22 Q21(a) and23 Q17(a) require the same full cosine-cycle sketch on supplied axes;21 Q26 asks two tangent roots without a sketch.22 Q21(b) requires two cosine roots, whereas23 Q17(b) uses a reflex restriction and one answer slot. QP locators:21p16,22p14,23p11; paired MS:21p10,22p11,23p7.

21 Q20 moves from independent bag picks to transfer-dependent composition;22 Q12 uses a supplied-data Venn diagram;23 Q25 conditions on odd totals in a sample-space table. These are distinct state/denominator requirements, not interchangeable probability routines. QP locators:21pp12–13,22p8,23p17; MS:21p9,22p8,23p9.

21 Q12 supplies sector perimeter and radius but withholds sector fraction;22 Q23 supplies angle/radius and an arc target to prove before forming a cone;23 Q19 directly contrasts minor-sector area and major-arc length from a shared60° diagram. QP:21p7,22p15,23p13; MS:21p7,22p12,23p8.

uncertainties: Bounded within-component comparison of three supplied October/November2025 variants only; no global difficulty ranking, route equivalence, lab suitability or syllabus exclusion inferred.

records.title: 0580 Paper 4 variant task demands

dimensions.observation: 42 Q8(a) requires drawing two images of original A, then Q8(b) identifying a supplied rotation. 43 Q7 requires descriptions of two already drawn images, including a negative enlargement. The same transformation component is assessed through production versus recognition. QP42 p6 and43 p6; MS42 p7 and43 p6.

42 Q18 derives a midpoint displacement AM from trapezium position vectors and a side ratio. 43 Q26 first requests an internal EF route, then introduces an undrawn intersection G of extended lines and requests CG. Supplied subpart count does not equal number of independent vector settings. QP42 p13 and43 p18; MS42 p10 and43 p10.

42 Q15(b) can follow through BC from Q15(a), while its final altitude calculation can use original dimensions directly. 43 Q18(a,b) use separate triangles sharing a supplied diagonal; the second angle does not require the first angle. QP42 p11 and43 p11; MS42 p9 and43 p8.

P4/41 Q24(c) asks both quadratic roots to two decimal places, then Q24(d) uses the positive physical speed to find one duration in hours and minutes. P4/42 Q19 instead requests two paired simultaneous-equation solutions. A printed "or" and multiple blanks must be interpreted through the requested solution set, not as permission to omit a root or a coordinate. Sources: QP41 p14/MS41 p10; QP42 p14/MS42 p10.

uncertainties: Source-based comparison candidate only; no approved lab alignment or claim of equivalent difficulty.

records.subject: mathematics
records.title: Logarithmic linearisation: exact coefficients and transformed data

dimensions.observation: P2/21 Q1 gives an exponential equation and y=mx+c target form, asking exact logarithm-ratio coefficients. P3/31 Q2 gives y³=Ae^(kx) and two coordinates on the described ln y against x line, asking numerical A and k. The latter coordinates are transformed ordinates, not original y-values; no plotted graph is supplied in either task.

Both tasks require two different constants without two printed slots. P2 asks slope/intercept themselves in a specified exact form. P3’s transformed slope/intercept are intermediates for the original model constants, requiring the factor3 and exponentiation when recovering A.

uncertainties: One task per component; bounded observed contrast, not a difficulty or prevalence ranking. Pure scope only.
